candidate.answerReason: If \(A=B=0\), the equation describes every point when \(C=0\) and no points otherwise. If \(B\ne0\), it can be solved for y; if \(B=0\) and \(A\ne0\), it gives the vertical line \(x=-C/A\). Thus A and B cannot both be zero, giving D.

methods.label: Apply the general-form condition
methods.explanation: When \(A\) and \(B\) are both 0, the equation is no longer a linear equation in \(x\) and \(y\) and cannot represent a line.
methods.levelReason: This is the defining coefficient condition for the general equation of a line.
